intent: Report where the user is in a Questionnaire, as a progressbar whose default text reads "Question X of Y".
typical_uses: A position line above the current question
A custom position display built from the position through `render`

dont_use_when.situation: A task's completion or a loading amount outside a questionnaire

invariants.text: The position counts only enabled items (the `items` entries when the root has `items`, otherwise the rendered enabled QuestionnaireItems), so a disabled item neither adds to the total nor takes a number.

The element carries role="progressbar" with aria-valuemin 1, aria-valuenow, aria-valuemax and aria-valuetext set from the position, is a polite live region, and is named "Questionnaire progress"; children replace only the visible text, never the aria values, and an `aria-label` replaces the name.

anti_patterns.dont: Compute the position yourself and pass it as text
anti_patterns.do_instead: Leave the default text, or read `current` and `total` from the state the function form of `render` receives; the root already owns the position

a11y.by: questionnaire.test.tsx asserts role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow "1" and aria-valuemax "3" and the text "Question 1 of 3"

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the progress's own state (`QuestionnaireProgressState`: current, first, last, total), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted.

good.title: A compact position drawn from the render state

bad.title: The kit Progress used as the questionnaire's position
bad.why: Progress knows nothing about the questionnaire; the count drifts as soon as an item is disabled or `items` changes, while QuestionnaireProgress reads the position from the root.

render.description: TS: RenderProp<QuestionnaireRootState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies.
